sections.content: How many people are "scaffolders, stagers and riggers"?

32,780 people

were counted on the census as "scaffolders, stagers and riggers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Scaffolders, stagers and riggers erect and dismantle scaffolding and working platforms, set up lifting equipment and ships� rigging, maintain and repair steeples, industrial chimneys and other tall structures and install, maintain and repair ropes, wires and cables.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "scaffolders, stagers and riggers" there were more men than women (99.2% compared with 0.8%).

This means "scaffolders, stagers and riggers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 99.2% and women made up 0.8% of "scaffolders, stagers and riggers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "scaffolders, stagers and riggers" included:

  • bricklayers
  • roofers, roof tilers and slaters
  • groundworkers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "scaffolders, stagers and riggers", 17.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "scaffolders, stagers and riggers" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "scaffolders, stagers and riggers" included:

  • legal professionals (other)
  • IT user support technicians
  • database administrators and web content technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "scaffolders, stagers and riggers", 5.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.8% compared with 8.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (61%) than self-employed (39%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Middlesbrough, this is in the region of the North East.
